intervals.label: commissioning
intervals.locator: phys.org, 4 February 2015; and Astropart. Phys. 108 (2019) 1-23, Sec. 3.2
intervals.note: The 2015 press release describes a planned spring/April 2015 switch-on (a schedule, not a confirmed event, hence marked planned). The detector paper documents that the first fill instead began around August 2016 and hit a contamination/seal problem (17 Aug 2016), with a second fill 'stably maintained since ... November 2016'. End date 2016-11 marks the transition to stable operation reported in the detector paper.
intervals.quote: This spring, scientists at SNOLAB will switch on a dark-matter detector that was designed and built at the University of Alberta.

intervals.label: second fill: science operations
intervals.locator: end: PASCOS 2025 slides "3 Year Dataset (Nov 2016 to March 2020)"; CAP 2026: "since the end of the second fill run in 2020"
intervals.note: The collaboration states that the second-fill data set ran from November 2016 to March 2020 (PASCOS 2025 slides) and that upgrades have been ongoing "since the end of the second fill run in 2020".
intervals.quote: has been stably maintained since completing the second fill in November 2016

intervals.label: detector upgrade (third fill)
intervals.locator: snolab.ca, DEAP-3600 experiment page, status field
intervals.note: SNOLAB's experiment page (read 2026-09-17; an Internet Archive capture of 25 May 2026 shows the same status) gives the status 'Upgrading'. No source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives the true start date of this phase; the start is set to 2026-09, the month this status was first read, as the earliest date the interval can be anchored to without inventing one -- it is not a claim that the upgrade began that month. A 2025 SNOLAB workshop community report (arXiv:2507.11368) is secondary reporting that associates recent work with a planned 'third fill'; its body text could not be retrieved and quoted, so no date from it is recorded. arXiv:2603.27372 (submitted 28 Mar 2026) corroborates ongoing 'hardware upgrades to mitigate residual challenging alpha-backgrounds for WIMP search'. The collaboration's abstracts of 22 June and 21 September 2026 describe a "just-started" / "newly initiated third fill run" with preliminary third-fill results, which conflicts with reading SNOLAB's "Upgrading" label as a current absence of data taking; this interval is therefore a phase annotation and not the detector's current state. The SNOLAB page no longer loads (HTTP 404 on 2026-10-25). A 2025 plan said third-fill data taking would end "~ summer 2026" with decommissioning to make room for ARGOlite; no source consulted says whether that happened.

intervals.label: detector upgrades (neck flow guides, particulate removal system)
intervals.note: Start = end of the second-fill data set (March 2020, month from the PASCOS slide); end = installation finished in February 2025. The fill and dust-removal procedures followed ("Upgrade done 2025-April / Filling continue 2025-July / Dust removal 2025-September" on the PASCOS 2025 timeline).
intervals.quote: The installation of these upgrades was finished in February 2025

intervals.label: third fill: science operations
intervals.locator: Light Dark World 2026 talk (30 July 2026), summary slide; outline slide: 'Now taking data with detector in the upgraded configuration'; slide 'WIMP search': 'New data taking with upgraded detector to mitigate backgrounds (2025 – present)'
intervals.note: Start month not found: the 2025 plan had "Data taking 2025-November" and the CAP 2025 abstract expected the fill to complete in August 2025; the 2026 abstracts call it "just-started" / "newly initiated". Whether third-fill data taking is still running on 2026-10-25 is not stated (the 2025 plan ended it "~ summer 2026"; SNOLAB lists "Upgrading"). The newest dated statement is a 30 July 2026 talk by a DEAP collaboration member: "Now taking data with detector in the upgraded configuration", "New data taking with upgraded detector to mitigate backgrounds (2025 – present)", "New data collection in progress with upgraded DEAP-3600 at SNOLAB". That shows third-fill running at the end of July 2026 and gives the start year (2025) but not the month; the 21 September 2026 abstract ("newly initiated third fill run", preliminary results) is consistent. No source dated after 21 September reports the end of the run, so the 2025 plan's "~ summer 2026" end is not confirmed. Confidence is 'approximate': a talk is a rank-12 source and the start year is approximate.
intervals.quote: New data collection in progress with upgraded DEAP-3600 at SNOLAB

name: DEAP-3600
notes: DEAP-3600 is a single-phase liquid argon SCINTILLATION detector, not a two-phase time projection chamber: it has no drift field and no ionization/charge readout, and detects only scintillation light via its 255 PMTs, using pulse-shape discrimination of that scintillation signal (deap3600.ca; Astropart. Phys. 108 (2019) 1-23, Sec. 1). technology_classes lists 'noble_liquid_tpc'/'argon_tpc' only because the ontology's technology-class list has no separate scintillator-only class; this should not be read as DEAP-3600 having TPC-style charge readout.

No proposal or approval interval is recorded: the INSPIRE experiment record (recid 1108195, read 2026-09-17) carries no date_proposed, date_approved or date_started fields, and no other source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives those dates.

summary.plain: DEAP-3600 is a dark matter experiment 2 km underground at SNOLAB in Canada. It watches 3.6 tonnes of liquid argon for the faint flash of light a dark matter particle would make hitting an argon nucleus. It has taken data since late 2016. After detector upgrades it began a third run, which the collaboration's abstract of 21 September 2026 describes as newly initiated.
summary.technical: Single-phase liquid argon scintillation detector (no drift field, no ionization/charge readout) at SNOLAB's 2 km level (6000 m.w.e.). Design target of 3600 kg LAr (~3300 kg maintained fill since Nov 2016), 1000 kg fiducial mass within a 55 cm radius, viewed by 255 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912-HQE PMTs. Sets the leading argon-target WIMP-nucleon exclusion limits above ~30 GeV/c² and searches for superheavy multi-scattering dark matter; after hardware upgrades since the end of the second fill (2020), a third fill with the upgraded detector was described as 'newly initiated' in the collaboration's abstract of 21 September 2026.
